title: French Onion Soup
headnote: Slowly caramelized onions simmered in rich beef broth and dry sherry, capped with garlic-rubbed French bread and bubbling Gruyère. “No one has ever complained that their French onion soup has too much cheese.” — Bob Mitchell

quotes.text: No one has ever complained that their French onion soup has too much cheese.
quotes.span: “No one has ever complained that their French onion soup has too much cheese.” — Bob Mitchell

items.raw: ¾ teaspoon kosher salt, divided, plus more to taste
2 cups grated Gruyère — more than you think

steps.text: Melt the butter in a heavy Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onions and ½ teaspoon salt, stir, cover, and let them soften for 5 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the onions are deeply caramelized and golden brown. This takes 1 to 2 hours and cannot be rushed.
Add the wine, sherry, and bay leaf and bring to a boil, scraping the bottom of the pot. Sprinkle the flour evenly over the top and stir well for 1 to 2 minutes as it thickens.
Slowly add the warm beef stock, the remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, and the pepper. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, then season to taste and remove the bay leaf.
Toast the bread slices until crisp, then rub the cut side of the raw garlic vigorously across the warm, rough surface.
Heat the broiler and arrange ovenproof soup crocks on a sturdy baking sheet.
Ladle the hot soup into the crocks, cover the tops with the garlic toasts, and pile on the Gruyère generously — you need more than you think.
Broil a few minutes, watching carefully, until the cheese is melted and bubbling with golden-brown spots. Serve immediately, and warn everyone that the crocks are very hot.

notes.label: Stock matters most
notes.text: this soup is onions and stock, so a thin broth shows. Use homemade or a good boxed beef stock.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: the soup is better made a day or two ahead and freezes for 3 months. Assemble and broil only at the last minute.

notes.label: No crocks
notes.text: ladle into bowls and broil the cheese toasts separately on a sheet pan, then float them on top.

notes.label: Onion type
notes.text: plain yellow onions caramelize best. Sweet onions have too much water.
